text_blocks.snippet: CANVAS (cerebellar ataxia, neuropathy, and vestibular areflexia syndrome) is primarily caused by a mutation in the RFC1 gene, specifically a biallelic expansion of the AAGGG repeat motif. This genetic mutation affects the way the body processes and uses genetic information, leading to the symptoms of CANVAS. In most cases, this mutation is inherited in an autosomal recessive manner, meaning that an individual needs to inherit two copies of the mutated gene (one from each parent) to develop the condition.
snippet_highlighted_words: a mutation in the RFC1 gene, specifically a biallelic expansion of the AAGGG repeat motif

list.title: The RFC1 Gene:
list.snippet: The RFC1 gene provides instructions for making a protein involved in DNA replication and repair.

list.title: AAGGG Repeat Expansion:
list.snippet: In CANVAS, there's an abnormal expansion of the AAGGG repeat sequence within the RFC1 gene, replacing the normal AAAAG sequence.

list.title: Biallelic Mutation:
list.snippet: This means that both copies of the RFC1 gene have the AAGGG repeat expansion.

list.title: Inheritance:
list.snippet: While CANVAS is often inherited in an autosomal recessive manner, meaning both parents carry the mutated gene, some cases can be sporadic, meaning the mutation arises spontaneously in the affected individual.

list.title: Symptoms:
list.snippet: The genetic mutation disrupts the normal function of the RFC1 gene, leading to a variety of neurological symptoms, including ataxia (lack of muscle coordination), neuropathy (nerve damage), and vestibular areflexia (loss of balance).

list.title: Other Potential Causes:
list.snippet: While the RFC1 gene mutation is the most common cause, there are other, rarer mutations in the RFC1 gene that can also lead to CANVAS.
